seoTitle: Free Press Release Template Generator Online
metaDescription: Fill in a few fields and get a standard press release with headline, dateline, quote, boilerplate and media contact. Free and runs in your browser.
intro: Fill in the company, headline, city, date, announcement, quote and contact details to get a press release in the standard structure, ready to edit.
why:
Journalists receive many releases a day and skim for the same elements: a clear headline, a dateline, the news in the first paragraph, a quote, the background and a contact. Writing from a blank page often buries the news under company history.

This template arranges your answers in the conventional order: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE, headline, city and date, what is being announced and why it matters, a quote, a link, the "About" paragraph, the media contact and the closing ###. It does not write the news for you, so keep the facts concrete and the language plain. Your text is assembled in the browser and not uploaded.
howTo: Fill in the company name, headline, city and date.
Write the announcement in one or two sentences, then add why it matters.
Add a quote with the speaker's name and title, a link, a press contact and the about text.
Copy the finished text and edit it into your own voice.

faq.q: What should the first paragraph contain?
faq.a: The news itself: who, what, when, where and why it matters, in one or two sentences. Put background after that. Many readers, and some journalists, will not get past the opening.

faq.q: How long should a press release be?
faq.a: Usually one page, around 300 to 500 words. The template produces a short skeleton, so expand the body only with facts the reader needs.

faq.q: Does it check facts or style?
faq.a: No. It only arranges what you type. Check names, dates and claims yourself, and avoid hype words that a journalist will cut anyway.

faq.q: Is the content saved or sent anywhere?
faq.a: No. The release is built in your browser and disappears when you close the page. Copy it into your own document if you want to keep it.
